title: Soft handoff protocol for dedicated-to-hosted tiering
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: When dedicated capacity becomes saturated or a node drain occurs, we need a deterministic, tenant-safe way to spill traffic to hosted while avoiding sudden latency/cost spikes and preserving tenant SLAs. Current hard-cutover approaches cause request amplifications, cache churn, and noisy telemetry which makes incident triage slow.

Goal: Implement a soft handoff protocol that gradually migrates sessions from dedicated pools to hosted backstops using probabilistic sampling, credit-based reservations, and progressive variant demotion so we achieve graceful degradation, predictable unit cost changes, and observable safety signals. This ticket covers design, config surface, implementation hooks in the routing adjudicator, and rollout plan.

Scope:
- New per-tenant soft-handoff config (thresholds, window, sample_rate, credit_budget) surfaced in the routing adjudicator.
- Integration with the capacity allocator to expose ephemeral reservation tokens that can be borrowed during a handoff window.
- Probability-based spillover: requests are diverted progressively rather than all-or-nothing.
- Model variant demotion policy that prefers cheaper quantized variants on hosted as load increases.
- Telemetry and SLOs: new metrics for handoff_rate, eviction_rate, observed_latency_delta, and cost_delta_by_tenant.
- Runbook and rollback steps for rapid remediation.

Out of scope: billing UI changes and long-term autoscaling policy tuning (handled in separate RFC).
acceptance_criteria: Routing adjudicator exposes 'soft_handoff' boolean and config blob per-tenant
When dedicated pool load > configured threshold, affected tenants should see a gradual increase in hosted routing up to sample_rate over the configured window
No single tenant should experience >15% p95 latency regression at handoff start; overall system p95 should stay within SLO target
Handed-off requests use demoted model variants on hosted if configured; fallback to higher-cost variant only if output-quality regression exceeds tolerance
Metrics appear in the Console (hand_off_rate, dedicated_to_hosted_count, handoff_latency_delta) and alert triggers for unexpected error spikes
Playbook verified in staging with synthetic tenant burst test and chaos node drain scenario
design_decisions: Use credit-based ephemeral reservations instead of immediate preemption to reduce thrash when dedicated capacity flaps
Probabilistic sampling (incremental ramp) preferred to deterministic eviction to maintain tail latency stability
Model variant demotion happens on the hosted side only to avoid modifying dedicated pool behavior
Expose conservative default configs per tier (enterprise vs dev) and allow overrides at tenant-level
Make the handoff mechanism reversible within the window: if capacity recovers, routing weight decays back to dedicated with hysteresis
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag gated behind 'soft_handoff' - implement behind runtime rollout flag
Phase 1: Internal dogfood - enable for internal tenants in us-west-2 at 0.5 sample_rate for 24h
Phase 2: Select beta customers (opt-in) with engineering support; observe metrics for 7 days
Phase 3: Gradual default enablement for P2/P3 tenants; monitor cost_delta and p95 latency for 30 days
Rollback: disable feature flag + purge reservations; immediate circuit-breaker if error rate increases >3x baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests for adjudicator sampling logic and reservation handshake
Integration test: simulate dedicated pressure and assert progressive hosted routing and metric emission
Load test: synthetic burst with 10 tenants at 5x normal QPS to validate no stability regression
Chaos test: kill 2/5 dedicated nodes during handoff and observe smooth migration and recovery
Quality gate: run sample output evals comparing demoted variant outputs to baseline to ensure acceptable degradation

2026-02-24 - Daniel Kim: Reviewed. Concern about double-counting cost when request touches both dedicated and hosted during retry — suggested adding request-level attribution id.
2026-03-01 - Maria Lopez: Design review notes — prefer exponential ramp rather than linear to reduce early-stage noise. Also recommended a safety cap per-tenant to avoid runaway costs.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented adjudicator sampling and reservation API prototype. Found edge case where KV cache warmup on hosted causes 200ms p95 blips; adding local cache hint to mitigate.
2026-03-09 - Priya Shah: QA in staging passed initial behavioral tests. Observed cost_delta of ~8% for test tenant at 30% sample rate; within expected range. Plan to enable dogfood on Monday.
2026-03-11 - SRE (notes): Alert rule added for handoff_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m. Recommended dashboard tile for per-tenant cost_delta.
